Senses.Explanation: Alert or wide-awake. The headword occurs 1,323 times in 275 allowlisted texts. One major deployment is the command “stay awake” or “stay alert” (惺惺著, 142 occurrences). Ruiyan Shiyan's case has him call “Master!” to himself, answer “Yes!”, then say, “Stay awake; after this do not be fooled by anyone” (主人公……諾……惺惺著，以後莫被人瞞). The same word describes an alert person: Tianyin Yuanxiu contrasts an alert person, for whom moving, not moving, or both are acceptable, with a person who is not alert, for whom none is acceptable (惺惺底人……未惺惺底人). A second major deployment is the fixed pair “still and alert” or “alert and still” (寂寂惺惺 / 惺惺寂寂, 47 / 35 occurrences). Yongjia Xuanjue's Verse on Stopping defines alert as not producing the signs of dull abiding or blank indeterminacy (惺惺謂不生昏住無記等相), then ranks alert-and-still as right, blank-and-still as wrong, still-and-alert as right, and scattered-and-alert as wrong (惺惺寂寂是，無記寂寂非，寂寂惺惺是，亂想惺惺非). Later records also criticize these deployments. Zhanran Yuancheng reports that all quarters called Ruiyan's self-address “playing with spirit-ghosts” (諸方謂其弄精魂). Fangrong Tongxi reverses the case by saying Ruiyan's house-master called Ruiyan rather than the reverse. Haiyin Zhaoru names still-and-alert among fetters, paired with torpor and scattering (被寂寂惺惺、昏沉散亂縛). The entry therefore keeps the attested gloss “alert” while preserving both the formulas and the named criticisms.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense, used of an alert condition and, by ordinary grammatical extension, of an alert person. The still-and-alert pairing is attributed to Yongjia Xuanjue's Verse on Stopping, while the Chan record also preserves criticism of Ruiyan Shiyan's command and names the pair itself as a fetter. The target remains the attested “alert” or “awake.” Compare “still” (寂寂), “master-in-charge” (主人公), and “playing with spirit-ghosts” (弄精魂).

Occurrences.Kwic: 一寂寂。二惺惺。寂寂謂不念外境善惡等事。惺惺謂不生昏住無記等相
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yongjia Collection of the Chan School (禪宗永嘉集), Verse on Stopping: Yongjia Xuanjue defines alert as not producing the signs of dull abiding or blank indeterminacy.

Occurrences.Kwic: 惺惺寂寂是。無記寂寂非。寂寂惺惺是。亂想惺惺非
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yongjia Collection of the Chan School (禪宗永嘉集), Verse on Stopping: Yongjia Xuanjue ranks alert-and-still and still-and-alert as right, while rejecting blank-and-still and scattered-and-alert.

Occurrences.Kwic: 唯永嘉既為惺惺寂寂、寂寂惺惺之說，以明均等
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄): the Yongzheng Emperor attributes the alert-and-still and still-and-alert formulation to Yongjia Xuanjue.

Occurrences.Kwic: 主人公，噯！惺惺著，以後莫被人瞞。諾！諸方謂其弄精魂
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhanran Yuancheng (湛然圓澄禪師語錄), in Zhanran Yuancheng's later raising of the Ruiyan case. Ruiyan Shiyan is the exact quoted speaker who calls to himself, answers, and says, ‘Stay alert; from now on do not be fooled by anyone.’ Zhanran Yuancheng then comments on the case; neither the record owner nor Yongjue Yuanxian speaks the stored quoted line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 昔瑞巖喚主人公惺惺著，今後莫被人瞞，良有以焉。諸方盡道瑞巖喚主人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fangrong Tongxi (方融璽禪師語錄) explicitly recalls Ruiyan Shiyan's self-address; Ruiyan is the exact earlier speaker of 'one in charge, stay alert,' and Fangrong comments on it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 寂寂惺惺、昏沉散亂，被寂寂惺惺、昏沉散亂縛
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Haiyin Zhaoru (海印昭如禪師語錄): Haiyin Zhaoru names still-and-alert among fetters, paired with torpor and scattering.

Occurrences.Kwic: 惺惺底人，動著亦得、不動著亦得、動著不動著亦得。未惺惺底人，動著不得、不動著不得、動著不動著總不得。
